title: OpenAgentCore: The OpenAI Agents API, open source and self-hosted
content:
The OpenAI Agents API, open source and self-hosted. Run Codex, Claude Code or MiniMax Code on your own machines with your own models, through the official OpenAI SDK.
Website · Documentation · Quickstart · Contributing
English · 简体中文
- Same API as OpenAI. Set OPENAI_BASE_URL and the official OpenAI SDK, or plain HTTP, works unchanged.
- Your agent, your model. Each Session runs Codex, Claude Code or MiniMax Code natively, as it runs on your machine, with the model provider you configure. See Harness capabilities.
- Compute that sleeps, workspaces that stay. On microsandbox, which keeps every workspace on independent storage, idle sandboxes release compute and resume on a compatible node with their files intact. E2B pauses idle sandboxes in place. Your own Linux, macOS or Windows machine also runs Sessions. See Sandbox Provider protocol.
- Replaceable parts. Sandbox Providers, workspace filesystems, Harnesses and model providers plug in through defined protocols.
Install Core, Web and PostgreSQL on Linux or macOS with Docker:
curl -fsSL https://openagentcore.dev/install.sh | bash
On Windows, in PowerShell:
irm https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/OpenAgentCore/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex
In Web, sign in with the Core key the installer prints, configure the public address, set a default model, issue a Project API key and add sandbox capacity (a node, E2B or OpenSandbox). Install Core and Web covers each step.
Then call it with the OpenAI SDK, with OPENAI_BASE_URL set to your API base URL (https://core.example/v1) and OPENAI_API_KEY to the Project API key:
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI()  # reads OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY
session = client.beta.agents.sessions.create(
    environment={"type": "openai_hosted"},
    input="Create /workspace/hello.txt with a short greeting, then describe it.",
    extra_body={"agent": {"x_agents_core": {"harness": "codex"}}},
)
print(session.id)
Run your first Session waits for the result and reads it back.
Applications and operators use these Core APIs:
Core keeps durable execution state. The Runtime runs the chosen Harness inside the Environment. Each connection is a defined protocol, so any part can be replaced on its own. See Architecture.
Read CONTRIBUTING.md before changing code. Report bugs and ask questions in GitHub Issues. Released under the MIT License.

report.summary: OpenAgentCore is MiniMax's MIT-licensed, self-hosted implementation of the OpenAI Agents API, letting teams run Codex, Claude Code or MiniMax Code agents on their own hardware and models through the unchanged official OpenAI SDK.
report.background: Coding agents have converged on a common shape: a CLI harness such as Codex or Claude Code, a sandbox to execute in, and a model behind it. In parallel, the OpenAI Agents/Responses API has become a de facto interface for agent sessions. The catch is that hosted offerings keep your prompts, repositories and workspace state on someone else's infrastructure and tie you to their model lineup. OpenAgentCore inverts that while staying wire-compatible. It arrives amid a broader splitting-apart of the agent stack — MCP for tool access, the OpenAI Agents SDK, and interchangeable sandbox runtimes like E2B and microsandbox — where the runtime layer is being decoupled from both the model vendor and the harness vendor.
key_points: Same API, no rewrites: point OPENAI_BASE_URL at your Core instance and set OPENAI_API_KEY to a Project key, and the official OpenAI SDK — or plain HTTP — works unchanged. Existing agent code keeps calling sessions.create and friends; only the base URL and key change, which makes migration close to a config edit rather than a porting project.

Your agent, your model: each Session natively runs Codex, Claude Code or MiniMax Code as it would run on your machine, but against whatever model provider you configure. The harness is selected per session via an extra_body field, so you can mix harnesses and route them to different providers inside one deployment.

Pluggable sandboxes with persistent workspaces: on microsandbox, every workspace sits on independent storage, idle sandboxes release compute and later resume on a compatible node with files intact; E2B pauses idle sandboxes in place. Your own Linux, macOS or Windows machine can also host Sessions, so you can start small and scale out.

Batteries-included install: a curl or PowerShell one-liner installs Core, a Web console and PostgreSQL via Docker. The Web UI walks operators through signing in with the Core key, setting the public address, picking a default model, issuing Project API keys and attaching sandbox capacity.

Replaceable by design: Sandbox Providers, workspace filesystems, Harnesses and model providers each connect through defined protocols, while Core holds durable execution state and the Runtime executes inside the Environment. Any single part can be swapped without touching the others, and the whole thing is MIT-licensed.
report.impact: For the industry, this is another step toward commoditizing the agent runtime layer: if the OpenAI agent API can be reimplemented and self-hosted, hosting stops being a moat and value shifts to models, harness quality and sandbox engineering. Expect similar clones and pressure on closed agent platforms to justify themselves on reliability and tooling rather than API surface. For developers, it means genuine portability — swap Codex for Claude Code or a local model without rewriting integration code — plus data residency and compliance options, at the cost of operating Postgres, sandbox nodes and the security posture that comes with running arbitrary agent code. For regular users, the effect is indirect: cheaper, more private agent products, and less risk that a single vendor's pricing or policy decides what their tools can do.
report.tools: Start with OpenAgentCore itself (GitHub: MiniMax-AI/OpenAgentCore) and its quickstart. Pair it with microsandbox or E2B for sandbox capacity, or OpenSandbox if you want to self-host the node layer. The harnesses worth installing alongside are Codex CLI, Claude Code and MiniMax Code. For client code, use the official OpenAI Python or JavaScript SDK, since compatibility is the whole point. Docker and PostgreSQL are prerequisites for the standard deployment.
